MAKABAYAN BLOC: COA, HINDI DPWH, ANG DAPAT MAG-AUDIT NG FLOOD CONTROL PROJECTS

We welcome the call to probe and audit flood control projects following the massive flooding that hit Metro Manila and surrounding areas despite the billions allocated for flood mitigation. However, we strongly oppose any move to let the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) conduct its own investigation.

"The DPWH cannot be trusted to investigate itself when it is neck-deep in these anomalies. This is like asking the fox to guard the henhouse," said House Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Rep. Antonio Tinio.

"Ang DPWH ay kasama sa problema, hindi bahagi ng solusyon. Paano nila i-audit ang sarili nilang kapalpakan? It would be a whitewash, pure and simple," added Assistant Minority Leader and Kabataan Rep. Renee Louise Co.

We call on the Commission on Audit (COA) to conduct a comprehensive audit of all flood control projects, similar to their work on the pork barrel scam and VP Sara Duterte's confidential funds. COA has proven its independence and capability in exposing government anomalies.

"COA has the technical expertise, independence, and constitutional mandate to conduct thorough audits. They exposed the PDAF scam, they questioned the confidential funds—they can certainly uncover the truth behind these flood control failures even by just basing from their previous audit reports," Tinio emphasized.

It can be recalled that during the 2025 budget deliberations, ACT Teachers grilled the DPWH on flood control issues, raising concerns about the effectiveness and transparency of their projects.

"Noong mga budget deliberations pa lang, pinupunto na namin ang mga kakulangan sa flood control projects. Now we see the catastrophic results—billions wasted while people suffer," Co stated.

"Hindi pwedeng magpatuloy ang culture of impunity sa DPWH. The people deserve answers, and only an independent body like COA can provide them," concluded the Makabayan lawmakers.

We urge Congress to pass a resolution directing COA to conduct an immediate and comprehensive audit of all DPWH flood control projects from 2016 to the present.

Royal Thai Army Brings Foreign Military Attachés and International Media to Observe Damage from Cambodian Attacks in Sisaket Province⁣
⁣
August 1, 2025 – The Royal Thai Army has taken a delegation of foreign military attachés, ambassadors, and international media to inspect the damage caused by Cambodian military attacks in several civilian areas of Sisaket Province, including a convenience store at a gas station, a school, and a Subdistrict Health Promoting.⁣
According to a Facebook post by the 2nd Army Region Command, the delegation departed at 08:30 AM from Wing 6 Military Airport in Don Mueang, led by Lt. Gen. Anupap Sirimonton, Deputy Chief of Staff of the Royal Thai Army; Air Chief Marshal Narat Boonprasert, Director-General of the Royal Thai Air Force’s Civil Affairs Department; Mr. Rasamee Chalichan, Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs; Maj. Gen. Naruedol Sukma, Chief Inspector General of the Royal Thai Army; and Maj. Gen. Prasert Muadchiangka, Director of the Foreign Affairs Bureau.⁣
⁣
The delegation, comprising 11 ambassadors, 26 military attachés from 22 countries, foreign and Thai media, and security officials, flew to Wing 21 in Ubon Ratchathani Province to observe and assess the impact of recent border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia.⁣
The Thai Army reported that Cambodian troops fired BM-21 rocket launchers and heavy artillery into civilian areas in Sisaket, violating the ceasefire agreement and causing extensive damage.⁣
The 22 participating countries included, among others:⁣
Malaysia, Myanmar, Japan, Brunei, Laos, Indonesia, the United States, Singapore, China, Vietnam, and the Philippines.⁣
Military attachés were present from countries such as:⁣
    1. Sweden⁣
    2. China⁣
    3. Malaysia⁣
    4. United States⁣
    5. Pakistan⁣
    6. Russia⁣
    7. Laos⁣
    8. Canada⁣
    9. Australia⁣
    10. France⁣
    11. Japan⁣
    12. Vietnam⁣
    13. Italy⁣
    14. Netherlands⁣
    15. Switzerland⁣
    16. Brunei⁣
    17. Indonesia⁣
    18. Yemen⁣
    19. Singapore⁣
    20. India⁣
    21. South Korea⁣
    22. Philippines, among others.⁣
⁣
The delegation then proceeded to the 22nd Military Circle at Sappasitthiprasong Camp in Warin Chamrap District, Ubon Ratchathani, for a briefing on the situation, particularly focused on Cambodia’s violations of the ceasefire agreement.⁣
⁣
Next, the group visited the damaged convenience store at a gas station in Ban Phue, Nong Ya Lat Subdistrict, Kantharalak District, which was hit by BM-21 rocket fire from Cambodian forces. The attack resulted in 8 deaths and 10 injuries.⁣
⁣
The delegation also visited Phum Srol Witthaya School in Sao Thong Chai Subdistrict to observe damage in the area, followed by an inspection at Sam Meng Subdistrict Health Promoting Hospital, which was heavily damaged by Cambodian artillery fire. The attack forced the evacuation of doctors and patients to safer locations. The hospital is currently non-operational due to the extent of the damage.⁣
⁣
Finally, the group visited an evacuation center in Kantharalak District to check on the condition and living arrangements of civilians displaced by the Cambodian attacks. The displaced residents were moved to safety after BM-21 rockets and artillery shells struck multiple civilian areas in the region.⁣
⁣
#TruthFromThailand #ไทยกัมพูชา #ThairathOnline
